difficulty_reason: For a finite morphism f : X -> S, the lemma identifies pseudo-coherence of f (as a morphism) with pseudo-coherence of f_* O_X as an O_S-module. The retained proof is written: the translation into algebra is displayed by the author — for a finite ring map R -> A, the map R -> A is pseudo-coherent (definition: A pseudo-coherent as an A-module relative to R, via polynomial presentations) if and only if A is pseudo-coherent as an R-module — and this is the finite case of the general More on Algebra comparison, lemma finite-extension-pseudo-coherent, which identifies pseudo-coherence over R and over A for complexes when A is finite over R; the relative-side-to-module-side dictionary is the chapter's own characterization lemma used in the definition unfolding. Retained author proof at lines 17461-17470.
